description: The plot illustrates how three accuracy-related metrics (Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy) vary as a function of Initial Confidence. The x-axis is labeled “Initial Confidence,” uses a linear scale, and spans approximately 0.86 to 1.00 with tick labels at about 0.86, 0.88, 0.89, 0.90, 0.91, 0.92, 0.93, 0.94, 0.95, 0.96, 0.97, 0.98, 0.99, and 1.00. The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 with major ticks at 0.0, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, and 1.0. The Final Accuracy series is a blue solid line with circular markers and vertical error bars; it starts near 0.93 at initial confidence 0.86, stays in the high 0.9s across the range, reaches about 1.00 around 0.98–0.99, and ends just under 1.0 (about 0.98) at 1.00. The Δ Accuracy series is an orange dashed line with diamond markers and error bars; it begins around 0.28 at 0.86, declines to roughly 0.12–0.14 around 0.90–0.91, rises to about 0.20 at 0.92, drops to its lowest values near 0.05–0.07 around 0.94–0.95, then increases again toward the right, ending around 0.20 at 1.00. The Initial Accuracy series is a green dash-dot line with square markers and error bars; it starts around 0.64 at 0.86, increases through about 0.76–0.85 by 0.89–0.91, dips near 0.77 at 0.92, rises to around 0.90–0.93 by 0.94–0.96, fluctuates slightly around the high 0.8s to low 0.9s through 0.99, and then drops to roughly 0.77 at 1.00.
